Task Guide:

Generate a symmetric tilt grain boundary (STGB) in an aluminum system using LAMMPS. The simulation should use metal units, and define a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice structure with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Define a three-dimensional simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. Create two atomic regions: an upper region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 1], y: [0 -1 3], z: [1 0 0]) and a lower region with lattice orientation (x: [0 3 -1], y: [0 1 3], z: [1 0 0]). Populate these regions with atoms according to their respective orientations to form a Σ5(310) symmetric tilt grain boundary. To remove unrealistic atomic overlaps, displace one region if necessary and delete overlapping atoms when the nearest neighbour distance is below a threshold of 0.35 Å. Compute relevant atomic properties, including centrosymmetry and per-atom potential energy, to assess the structural quality of the generated grain boundary. Perform an initial energy minimization using the conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with energy and force tolerances of 1e-15 and a maximum of 5000 iterations. Save the minimized configuration in a dump file. Conduct a second energy minimization while allowing the simulation box to relax in the direction perpendicular to the grain boundary to ensure an energetically stable configuration. Save the final minimized structure using the write_data command in LAMMPS data format. Calculate the grain boundary energy using a reference bulk energy per atom of −3.360000 eV. Compute the total system energy, subtract the bulk energy contribution, and normalize by the grain boundary area. Convert the result to mJ/m² and round the final value. As the final output, return the computed grain boundary energy in mJ/m². Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_10/task_10_trial_1 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

function.arguments:
{"path": "/results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_10/task_10_trial_1/gb_al.in", "content": "# LAMMPS input script for Aluminum Σ5(310) STGB
units metal
dimension 3
boundary p p p
atom_style atomic

# Create lattice and regions
lattice fcc 4.05
region box block 0 30 0 30 0 30
create_box 1 box
create_atoms 1 region box

# Define upper and lower regions with orientations
region upper block 0 30 15 30 0 30
region lower block 0 30 0 15 0 30

# Set orientations
orient upper x 0 3 1 y 0 -1 3 z 1 0 0
orient lower x 0 3 -1 y 0 1 3 z 1 0 0

# Potential
pair_style eam/alloy
pair_coeff * * /potentials/EAM/Al99.eam.alloy Al

# Delete overlapping atoms
delete_atoms overlap 0.35 upper lower

# Compute properties
compute csym all centro/atom fcc
compute pe all pe/atom

# First minimization
minimize 1e-15 1e-15 5000 5000
dump min1 all custom 1 dump.min1.lammpstrj id type x y z c_csym c_pe

# Second minimization with box relaxation
fix boxrelax all box/relax y 0 vmax 0.001
minimize 1e-15 1e-15 5000 5000
unfix boxrelax

# Save final configuration
write_data final_gb.data

# Calculate energies for GB energy
variable E_bulk equal -3.360000  # eV/atom
variable N_atoms equal count(all)
variable E_total equal pe
variable E_gb equal (v_E_total - v_N_atoms*v_E_bulk)/(2*lx*lz)*16021.7733  # Convert to mJ/m²

print "GB_energy ${E_gb}""}
